content: Pyrantel pamoate is an anthelmintic medication approved by the FDA for the treatment of pinworm infections. It is available in suspension form and is dosed based on body weight. Common side effects include diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, headache, and drowsiness. For adults, the FDA-approved dosage of Pyrantel pamoate suspension is as follows: For individuals weighing 63-87 lbs (29-39 kg): 1.5 teaspoonfuls (7.5 mL). For individuals weighing 88-112 lbs (40-50 kg): 2 teaspoonfuls (10.0 mL). For individuals weighing 113-137 lbs (51-62 kg): 2.5 teaspoonfuls (12.5 mL). For individuals weighing 138-162 lbs (63-73 kg): 3 teaspoonfuls (15.0 mL). For individuals weighing 163-187 lbs (74-84 kg): 3.5 teaspoonfuls (17.5 mL). For individuals weighing 188 lbs (85 kg) or more: 4 teaspoonfuls (20.0 mL). Off-label uses in adults include treatment for ascariasis, Moniliformis infections, Uncinaria infections, and trichostrongyliasis. The dosage for these conditions is typically 11 mg/kg, with variations in frequency and duration depending on the specific infection. For pediatric patients aged 2 to 12 years, the FDA-approved dosage is also based on body weight: For children under 25 lbs (11 kg) or under 2 years old: Use only under physician guidance. For children weighing 25-37 lbs (11-16 kg): 0.5 teaspoonful (2.5 mL). For children weighing 38-62 lbs (17-28 kg): 1 teaspoonful (5.0 mL). For children weighing 63-87 lbs (29-39 kg): 1.5 teaspoonfuls (7.5 mL). For children weighing 88-112 lbs (40-50 kg): 2 teaspoonfuls (10.0 mL). For children weighing 113-137 lbs (51-62 kg): 2.5 teaspoonfuls (12.5 mL). For children weighing 138-162 lbs (63-73 kg): 3 teaspoonfuls (15.0 mL). For children weighing 163-187 lbs (74-84 kg): 3.5 teaspoonfuls (17.5 mL). For children weighing 188 lbs (85 kg) or more: 4 teaspoonfuls (20.0 mL). Off-label pediatric uses include treatment for ascariasis, Moniliformis infections, Uncinaria infections, and trichostrongyliasis, with similar dosing regimens to those used in adults. Pyrantel pamoate is contraindicated in pregnant individuals and those with liver disease. It is classified as Pregnancy Category C by the FDA and Category B2 by the Australian Drug Evaluation Committee, indicating that there is insufficient data on its safety during pregnancy. There is no specific guidance on its use during labor and delivery, in nursing mothers, or in geriatric, renal-impaired, or immunocompromised patients. The medication is administered orally, and there is no information available regarding its use via intravenous routes. In cases of overdose, immediate medical attention should be sought, and the National Poison Help hotline (1-800-222-1222) should be contacted. The mechanism of action, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, and nonclinical toxicology of Pyrantel pamoate are not well-documented in the drug label. The medication is supplied as a suspension in 32 fl oz (946 mL) bottles and should be stored at a temperature of 20°–25°C (68°–77°F). Pyrantel pamoate is marketed under brand names such as Ascarel, Pamix, and Pin-X. There is no established interaction between Pyrantel pamoate and alcohol, but patients are advised to consult their healthcare provider regarding alcohol consumption while taking this medication.
